statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-7210: xml.parsers.expat and xml.etree.ElementTree seeded Expat's hash-flooding protection with too little entropy, so a crafted XML document could trigger hash flooding. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/149018 (3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/e37df2a6a71d6538698e2d3188a7c345b827640b), first released in CPython 3.12.14; full mitigation also needs Expat 2.8.0 or later, because the 16-byte salt call exists only there. See https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-7210. Checked the pyexpat extension module in the python-3.12 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. pyexpat links the system libexpat. From 3.12.14-r1 on it imports XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes, so it uses the 16-byte salt and only loads against libexpat 2.8.0 or later; no earlier build references that function. The range ends at 3.12.14-r1.

CVE-2026-7210: xml.parsers.expat and xml.etree.ElementTree seeded Expat's hash-flooding protection through XML_SetHashSalt() with too little entropy, so a crafted XML document could still trigger hash flooding. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/149018 (3.14 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/eeea765cb9d8f1fc3d8918b272ac3c477983f27a), first released in CPython 3.14.6: when built against Expat 2.8.0 or later, pyexpat seeds each parser with a 16-byte salt through XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes(), and the advisory says full mitigation needs both this change and Expat 2.8.0 or later. See https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/PNY5OMBDPM2FRUZTWFFPJ6LISWKV627K/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-7210. In the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package the pyexpat extension module links the system libexpat (NEEDED libexpat.so.1). Checked its dynamic symbol imports in every published build of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package, 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r4, on x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.5-r9 import only XML_SetHashSalt. 3.14.6-r9, the first CPython 3.14.6 build, and every later build also import XML_SetHashSalt16Bytes, so they use the 16-byte salt and need a libexpat that provides it (2.8.0 or later). The range ends at 3.14.6-r9.

See https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-7210. Checked the pyexpat extension module in the standard library shipped by these packages (libpython-3.12-stdlib and libpython-3.12-minimal) in every build published in the DHI Debian repository, 3.12.13-0 to 3.12.16-7, amd64 and arm64; both architectures agree. These packages build pyexpat with the copy of Expat bundled in CPython: its version string is expat_2.7.4 in 3.12.13-0 to 3.12.13-13, which predates the 16-byte salt, and expat_2.8.3 or later from 3.12.14-0, which is built from CPython 3.12.14 (its standard library files match the v3.12.14 release) and so compiles the 16-byte salt path. The range ends at 3.12.14-0.
